name: Elbow (envelope example)
_WHAT_THIS_IS: The same joint as elbow_profile_example, sized against a MEASURED session instead
A profile is a designer's guess at one simple move, repeated forever. A
real joint runs a mix of tasks, payloads and idle periods whose torque
distribution looks nothing like one trapezoid, so sizing against the guess
is over-confident exactly where it matters most: thermal.
Both blocks are present on purpose. The envelope wins -- see the
precedence note below -- and the report names the profile as superseded
rather than silently ignoring it. Delete the 'envelope' key, or set
motion_source to 'profile', and this file falls straight back to the
commanded-motion path with no other edits.

ratio.note: actuators mounted coaxially on the joint, no extra reduction

_MOTION_AND_LOAD: READ THIS BEFORE THE load BLOCK BELOW. It decides whether any of it is used.
Three ways to declare how this joint moves, highest wins:
envelope  > profile > duty_segments
An envelope is a record of what the joint ACTUALLY did, so it supersedes a
profile, which is a guess at one simple move; a profile in turn supersedes
duty_segments, which is a hand-written segment list with no solver behind
it. Declaring several is fine and expected: the superseded blocks are kept
so that removing the higher one falls back rather than erroring.
Set motion_source to pin one explicitly -- envelope | profile |
duty_segments | auto (the default). Pinning a block you have not defined
is an error, not a silent fallback, because the whole point of pinning is
to be certain which input you are looking at. --motion-source on the
command line overrides this for a single run, which is how you A/B the
commanded profile against the measured envelope without editing anything.
WHICH DECIDES WHETHER load IS USED AT ALL. The two loading models are
mutually exclusive:
load + profile   the torque history is PREDICTED from the mass
properties, gravity, friction and the commanded move.
Every field in load is used.
envelope         the torque history was OBSERVED. Gravity, friction and
external torque were all acting on the real joint while
it ran, so they are already inside the logged numbers.
NOTHING in load is read -- not even the mass properties.
Re-applying them would double-count.
THIS FILE IS ENVELOPE-DRIVEN, so the whole load block below is currently
inert: edit any of it and the report does not change. The one visible
consequence is the Inertia ratio check, which reports as not available
rather than quoting a figure the measurement cannot corroborate.
It is kept, and kept honest, because deleting the envelope key or running
--motion-source profile falls straight back to the predicted path and every
field goes live again with no other edit. Try it:
./eval_actuator.py -a robstride_00 -j elbow_envelope_example \
--motion-source profile

load._note: INERT while the envelope above is active -- see _MOTION_AND_LOAD. Used in full on the profile path.

total_mass_at_CG.note: whole moving assembly: link, bracket, hardware and anything carried

distance_joint_axis_to_CG.note: joint axis to the CG. Counts linearly for gravity and SQUARED for inertia

moment_of_inertia_around_CG.note: about the CG, NOT about the joint axis -- the parallel-axis transfer m*d^2 is added for you

joint_plane_tilt.note: profile path only: scales how much of gravity this joint's plane sees

gravity_angle.note: joint angle at which the CG points straight DOWN, in the same frame as profile.stroke_start. Profile path only -- an envelope needs no gravity angle, because the gravity torque is already in the log. NOT related to the envelope's sign_convention, which is a separate question about which way the logger's positive torque points

envelope.note: one hour of pick-and-place on cell 3, three payload variants

profile._note: SUPERSEDED by the envelope above; kept so this file falls back cleanly

bus_voltage.note: 13S lithium pack, nominal 48.1 V, 54.6 V at full charge

T_ambient.note: inside the arm shell, NOT room temperature

max_surface_temp.note: housing is reachable by the operator; set from your own safety case
